config.title: Grid row/column span

intro.title: Grid row/column span
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage layout using CSS Grid to arrange items into rows and columns. You will learn how to use the grid-column and grid-row properties to make elements span across multiple grid tracks. The core concept involves controlling the placement and size of grid items by specifying start and end lines. This will help you create more complex and flexible layouts with CSS Grid.
intro.usecase: Grid row and column spanning is essential for creating complex layouts in modern web applications. You'll use this technique when building dashboard interfaces where widgets need to occupy multiple grid cells, such as a large analytics chart spanning two columns while smaller metrics cards fit in single columns. Product galleries often employ column spans to feature highlighted items prominently, while news websites use row spans for featured articles that stretch across multiple rows. This pattern gives you precise control over component placement in responsive grid systems without disrupting the overall layout structure.

objectives: Apply the grid-column property to span elements across multiple columns
Implement the grid-row property to extend elements across several rows
Configure grid items with span notation to control their placement
Construct grid layouts by manipulating item spanning behavior
Integrate row and column spanning to create complex grid structures
Update existing grid layouts by adjusting span values
Initialize grid containers with specific tracks and span items accordingly

steps.title: Create a grid container with basic grid properties
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule for a class named .grid-container that sets up a grid with 3 columns and 3 rows, each 100px in size, and a 10px gap between items.
steps.hint: Use display: grid to create the container, grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows with repeat() to define the tracks, and gap for spacing.
steps.expectedOutcome: A .grid-container class is defined with display: grid, grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 100px), grid-template-rows: repeat(3, 100px), and gap: 10px.
successCriteria: The .grid-container class includes display: grid, grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 100px), grid-template-rows: repeat(3, 100px), and gap: 10px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but some properties are missing or incorrect. Make sure to include display: grid, grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 100px), grid-template-rows: repeat(3, 100px), and gap: 10px.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid container isn't set up correctly. Review the instruction: you need to create a .grid-container class with display: grid, grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 100px), grid-template-rows: repeat(3, 100px), and gap: 10px.

steps.title: Create HTML structure with numbered grid items
steps.instruction: Create a div with class 'grid-container' containing 9 divs with class 'grid-item' numbered 1 through 9
steps.hint: You'll need to write HTML markup with a container div and 9 child divs, each with text content showing their number.
steps.analogousExample:

2
3
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll see a grid container with 9 numbered grid items ready to be styled with CSS Grid properties.
successCriteria: HTML contains a div with class 'grid-container' and 9 child divs with class 'grid-item' numbered 1-9
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have exactly 9 numbered grid items inside the container div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HTML structure isn't quite right. You need a container div with class 'grid-container' containing 9 child divs with class 'grid-item', each showing a number from 1 to 9.

steps.title: Apply column span to a specific grid item
steps.instruction: Create a new CSS rule for a class named '.span-column' that uses the 'grid-column: span 2' property to make an item span two columns.
steps.hint: Add a new CSS rule that starts with '.span-column' and contains the 'grid-column' property set to 'span 2'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule for the .span-column class is created with the grid-column property set to span 2.
successCriteria: The .span-column class is defined with the property grid-column: span 2.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your .span-column rule includes 'grid-column: span 2' exactly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .span-column class is missing or doesn't have the correct grid-column property.

steps.title: Apply row span to a different grid item
steps.instruction: Create a CSS class named '.span-row' that uses the grid-row property to make an item span two rows.
steps.hint: Use the grid-row property with the value 'span 2' to make an element span two rows vertically.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS class .span-row is created with grid-row: span 2 to enable row spanning.
successCriteria: The .span-row class is defined with the property grid-row: span 2.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your .span-row class includes 'grid-row: span 2'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .span-row class is missing or doesn't have the correct grid-row property.

steps.title: Apply both row and column span to another item
steps.instruction: Create a new CSS class named '.span-both' that uses both 'grid-column: span 2' and 'grid-row: span 2' properties.
steps.hint: Add a new CSS rule that defines both grid-column and grid-row properties with span values.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS class will be created that applies both column and row spanning to grid items.
successCriteria: The .span-both class is defined with both grid-column: span 2 and grid-row: span 2 properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your .span-both class includes both 'grid-column: span 2' and 'grid-row: span 2' properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .span-both class should contain both grid-column and grid-row properties with span values.

steps.title: Use explicit grid line numbers for column spanning
steps.instruction: Create a new CSS class named .explicit-column that uses the grid-column property with explicit line numbers: grid-column: 1 / 3;
steps.hint: Add a new CSS rule that targets the .explicit-column class and sets its grid-column property to span from grid line 1 to grid line 3.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS class .explicit-column is created that uses explicit grid line numbers for column spanning.
successCriteria: The .explicit-column class exists with the property grid-column: 1 / 3;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your .explicit-column class has the exact property grid-column: 1 / 3;
steps.feedbackWrong: The .explicit-column class is missing or doesn't have the correct grid-column property. Try creating a new CSS rule with grid-column: 1 / 3;

steps.title: Use explicit grid line numbers for row spanning
steps.instruction: Create a CSS class named .explicit-row that uses grid-row: 2 / 4 to span from grid line 2 to line 4.
steps.hint: Add a new CSS rule with the selector .explicit-row and set the grid-row property to 2 / 4.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS class .explicit-row is created with grid-row: 2 / 4 to demonstrate explicit row spanning using grid line numbers.
successCriteria: The .explicit-row class is defined with grid-row: 2 / 4.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your .explicit-row class has the correct grid-row property value of 2 / 4.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .explicit-row class is missing or doesn't have the correct grid-row property. Try creating a new CSS rule with .explicit-row and grid-row: 2 / 4.

steps.title: Apply spanning classes to specific HTML elements
steps.instruction: Add the class 'span-column' to the grid item with the number 4 in your HTML structure.
steps.hint: Look for the HTML element that contains the number 4 and add the class attribute with the value 'span-column'.
steps.analogousExample: Item content
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid item with number 4 will visually span across multiple columns when you view the page.
successCriteria: The HTML element containing the number 4 has the class attribute with value 'span-column'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're adding the class to the correct grid item (number 4).
steps.feedbackWrong: The class wasn't applied correctly. Check that you're adding 'span-column' to the div containing the number 4.

steps.title: Add visual indicators for spanned items
steps.instruction: Add a distinct background color to the .span-both class to make it visually stand out from regular grid items.
steps.hint: Use the background-color property with a bright color like gold or coral.
steps.expectedOutcome: The item with both row and column span will have a distinct background color, making it clearly visible.
successCriteria: The .span-both class includes a background-color property with a distinct color value.
